newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik peace-making body to meet by July 7.
newsitem.headline: Tajik peace-making body to meet by July 7.

text.p: A special reconciliation commission will meet within a week to prepare a new order in Tajikistan after four years of civil war, a United Nations official said on Tuesday.

"The first meeting of the National Commission for Reconciliation should take place by July 7. This first meeting will take place in Moscow," U.N. Representative in Tajikistan Gerd Dietrich Merrem told a news conference.
He said the main issue on the agenda would be the announcement of an amnesty for all participants in the civil war, which killed tens of thousands of people in the former Soviet republic.
Last Friday in Moscow, Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and Islamic opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri signed a final peace agreement for the Central Asian state of 5.7 million people.
In line with the agreement -- brokered by Russia, Iran and the United Nations -- Rakhmonov remains president but 30 percent of government posts must be given to the opposition.
Nuri will chair the 26-member National Commission for Reconciliation, in which places will be divided equally between each side.
The commission must work out constitutional changes and prepare elections for a new parliament, which must take place before the end of 1998.
Both sides will also have to work out the procedure for a first exchange with prisoners -- 50 on each side -- due to take place by July 15, Merrem added.
